name: Nethinim
overview: The Nethinim were a distinct group within Israel's returned exiles, serving as devoted assistants to the Levites and fulfilling roles such as hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and the altar, as established by Joshua (Joshua 9:27). Their origins likely trace back to the appointment of the Gibeonites and the remnant of Canaanites whom Solomon subjected to bondservice (1 Kings 9:20-21). They were numerous, exempted from tribute, organized under their own leaders, and resided in designated cities alongside Israelites, priests, and Levites (1 Chronicles 9:2; Ezra 2:43-44). The Nethinim demonstrated zeal for the covenant through their faithful service in the post-exilic community.
